external_entities.name: Duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who opens the dispatch console in a browser.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.
external_entities.notes: The method by which an engineer signs in to the console is not recorded.

external_entities.name: Scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work through a SOAP feed.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.notes: The partner's identity mechanism for the importer is not recorded.

processes.name: Browser
processes.description: The browser used by duty engineers to open the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.
processes.notes: The browser technology and security properties are not described.

processes.name: Corporate web host
processes.description: The corporate web host that serves the dispatch console application.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it
processes.notes: The host's location, technology, exposure, and security controls are not described.

processes.name: Dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript application used by duty engineers.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it. The API's allowed CORS origins and credential policy are also not recorded.

processes.name: Dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer to manage dispatch work.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
processes.notes: The API's allowed CORS origins and whether it allows credentials are not recorded.

processes.name: Schedule importer
processes.description: A process that pulls the partner's planned work, parses XML, archives the downloaded documents, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: Nothing was written down about how the partner identifies the importer or how the importer identifies the partner. The API token was issued when the importer was built and has not been rotated.

data_stores.name: Dispatch database
data_stores.description: A database holding job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order carries the token or session that created it, and nothing about the person behind that token. How the database is protected at rest is not written down anywhere.

data_stores.name: Schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder containing each document downloaded from the scheduling partner.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive
data_stores.notes: The archive is described as a folder on the corporate file store. Its protection and classification are not recorded.

data_stores.name: Corporate file store
data_stores.description: The corporate file store containing the schedule archive folder.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a folder on the corporate file store
data_stores.notes: Its location, technology, classification, and protection at rest are not described.

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.
data_flows.notes: The engineer's sign-in method is not recorded.

data_flows.name: load console
data_flows.description: The browser loads the dispatch console application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.

data_flows.name: serve app
data_flows.description: The corporate web host serves the dispatch console application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The API answers the console cross-origin. The allowed origins and credential policy are not recorded.

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and holds a WebSocket to receive live job status from the dispatch API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: It is not recorded whether the socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the engineer's session again after opening.

data_flows.name: read-write database
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: Job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: pull planned work
data_flows.description: The schedule importer pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: The partner's identification of the importer and the importer's identification of the partner are not recorded.
data_flows.data_description: Tomorrow's planned work in an XML document

data_flows.name: write archive
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive
data_flows.data_description: Downloaded XML documents containing planned work

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: The importer presents an API token. The token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers and the schedule importer are located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: Production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company zone holding the live estate, with authority to move a crew and change the work a depot does that day.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: Scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the scheduling partner, which is another company.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API presents a web interface because the source describes cross-origin API access and a WebSocket endpoint.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the console calls the API cross-origin and opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API.
